title: indigo_libs: aux base class defines the weather condition, threshold and safety properties; cloudwatcher and simulator use them
description:
Requested by the owner on 2026-11-23.

Today AUX_HUMIDITY, AUX_WIND, AUX_RAIN, AUX_CLOUD, AUX_SKY, their *_THRESHOLDS and AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY are defined by each weather driver, with different types: aux_cloudwatcher uses read-only switch vectors (AT_MOST_ONE, the active level ON), aux_simulator uses light vectors (active level OK for the best level, ALERT otherwise). The aux base class (indigo_libs/indigo_aux_driver.c, indigo_aux_driver.h) currently defines no properties and has no context.

Change:
1. The aux base class defines these properties: AUX_HUMIDITY (HUMID, NORMAL, DRY), AUX_WIND (STRONG, MODERATE, CALM), AUX_RAIN (RAINING, WET, DRY), AUX_CLOUD (CLEAR, CLOUDY, OVERCAST), AUX_SKY (DARK, LIGHT, VERY_LIGHT), AUX_HUMIDITY_THRESHOLDS, AUX_WIND_THRESHOLDS, AUX_RAIN_THRESHOLDS, AUX_CLOUD_THRESHOLDS, AUX_SKY_THRESHOLDS and AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY. All are hidden by default; a weather driver unhides those it supports and sets threshold ranges, defaults and units. Follow the pattern of the other base classes (context struct with property pointers and macros in indigo_aux_driver.h; definition and deletion with the connection, threshold changes handled and saved with the configuration in the base class; detach releases them). Generated drivers use them as 'inherited' properties; no generator change is expected. If the generator turns out to need a change, stop and ask the owner first (AGENTS.md).
2. The condition properties become read-only light vectors with new semantics: the item of the current level is OK and all other items are IDLE (e.g. AUX_RAIN while raining: RAINING OK, WET IDLE, DRY IDLE; while wet: WET OK, others IDLE).
3. The property state of a condition property reports the sensor: OK = the sensor operates normally, ALERT = no valid reading, IDLE = the sensor is not present (all items IDLE then).
4. AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY keeps its current items and contract (indigo_aux_evaluate_weather_safety / indigo_aux_update_weather_safety); only its definition moves to the base class. The unsafe level of each condition (STRONG, RAINING, OVERCAST, HUMID) is now read from the light of that item instead of a switch.
5. aux_cloudwatcher and aux_simulator drop their own definitions of these properties and use the inherited ones (edit the .driver files, regenerate). Behaviour of the thresholds and classification stays as documented; only the type and the light/state semantics change. Bump both driver versions.
6. Update indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md (aux base class section, both driver sections), the tests of both drivers (indigo_test/integration/test_aux_simulator.c, test_aux_cloudwatcher_simulator.c), test_agent_auxiliary_simulator.c if affected, and unit tests of the base class where useful.

aux_skyalert adopting these properties is a separate sub-ticket.

Compatibility: clients reading AUX_WIND/AUX_RAIN/AUX_CLOUD/AUX_HUMIDITY/AUX_SKY of aux_cloudwatcher as switches will see light vectors; this is accepted by the owner.

outcome.summary:
Independent review of master...eb97bf326. No blocking defects found.

Verified:
- Base class (indigo_libs/indigo_aux_driver.c/.h): context allocated only when device_context is NULL, the same pattern as the focuser and other base classes. All 11 properties start hidden. Hidden properties are never defined or deleted (indigo_define/delete skip hidden), never changeable (match_changeable needs defined) and never saved (indigo_save_property skips hidden). So the 40+ other indigo_aux_attach users (aux_*, dome_dragonfly, focuser/rotator_lunatico, focuser_prodigy, focuser_steeldrive2, mount_lx200, mount_synscan, system_alpaca*, aux_asiair, aux_rpio) define nothing extra. A grep found no AUX_* macro, AUX_CONTEXT or AUX_*_GROUP collisions in indigo_drivers, indigo_linux_drivers, indigo_mac_drivers, indigo_optional_drivers, indigo_server, indigo_tools or indigo_test. No aux user sets device_context before attach; alpaca only checks it for NULL on attach failure. Detach releases each property once; the regenerated drivers no longer release them. CONNECTION falls through to indigo_device_change_property as before. CONFIG save writes the thresholds before the device base class writes the file.
- Light semantics: indigo_aux_set_condition makes the level OK and the others IDLE only for OK, otherwise all items IDLE, and sets the state as given. Cloudwatcher: OK on a valid reading, IDLE when the anemometer or RH sensor is absent, ALERT on a failed poll or a missing reading. Simulator: always OK with a level.
- AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY: the unsafe flag is read from light==OK of OVERCAST/RAINING/STRONG/HUMID. agent_auxiliary reads only AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY.
- Generator: indigo_tools is unchanged. Both drivers regenerate byte-identically (.c, .h, _main.c) with the unchanged generator. Versions bumped 17->18 and 2->3. Inherited blocks follow AGENTS.md: cloudwatcher has no on_change for thresholds, so the base class handles them; the simulator keeps on_change for immediate reclassification.
- T

Round 2 review of eb97bf326..6bce62d16 plus consistency of the whole master...HEAD diff. No defects found.
- README: master...HEAD changes only indigo_drivers/aux_simulator/README.md line 8, exactly the approved sentence (current level OK, other items IDLE, property state shows the sensor).
- on_disconnect (indigo_aux_simulator.driver:440-448): no return, no blank lines, single-line calls, braces; it runs after indigo_cancel_pending_handlers() and before the generator's silent BUSY->OK reset loop, so it adds the missing client update without duplicating generator work. Simulator version 17->18 (bumped once in this ticket), cloudwatcher 2->3.
- Regeneration: running the unchanged build/bin/indigo_generator (indigo_tools has no diff) on both .driver files in a scratch dir reproduces the checked-in .c, .h and _main.c byte for byte.
- Tests catch the defects: a mutant aux_simulator.c with the weather.on_disconnect block removed makes weather_threshold_change_cancelled_by_disconnect fail at test_aux_simulator.c:494 (threshold stays BUSY), other cases unaffected. weather_thresholds_saved_by_config and thresholds_saved_by_config would fail if the base class did not save thresholds: the client cache is released on teardown, so the restored value cannot be a stale cache hit; the simulator case also checks the restored threshold classifies a reading and restores the default.
- Determinism: queue blocking uses atomic flags with bounded waits and releases the queue on every path.
- Isolation: both suites use indigo_test_use_private_home()/indigo_test_remove_private_home(); no file under ~/.indigo changed during the runs and no /tmp/indigo-test-home.* directory remained.
- Runs in the worktree: test_aux_simulator all passed (57 s, alarm 90 s), test_aux_cloudwatcher_simulator 0 failing scenarios (192 s), test_agent_auxiliary_simulator all passed (13 s). git diff --check clean.
Non-blocking note: thresholds_saved_by_config (test_aux_cloudwatcher_simulator.c:745) leaves RAIN WET=15

Combined-tree review (6bce62d16..c894f1043 and master...HEAD). (1) The sub-ticket commit c894f1043 touches only aux_skyalert files (driver, generated .c, README, host simulator, test), the aux_skyalert section of indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md and the aux_skyalert row of MIGRATION_STATUS.md; no file or section of ticket 1 changed. Generator source unchanged against master. (2) PROPERTIES.md: base-class section (11 properties, hidden by default, thresholds always defined and CONFIG-saved, conditions and AUX_WEATHER_SAFETY connection-only, light/state semantics) agrees with the cloudwatcher, simulator and skyalert sections; skyalert threshold labels, ranges and defaults in the section match indigo_aux_skyalert.driver (humidity 0-100 90/70, wind 0-1024 1024/1024, rain 800/950, cloud -20/-10, sky 250/750); groups agree with AUX_WEATHER_GROUP/AUX_THRESHOLDS_GROUP in indigo_aux_driver.c. (3) Freshly compiled unchanged indigo_tools/indigo_generator.c regenerates indigo_aux_cloudwatcher, indigo_aux_simulator and indigo_aux_skyalert .c/.h/_main.c byte-identical to the checked-in files. (4) README diffs on master...HEAD are only aux_simulator line 8 and the aux_skyalert '## Comments' -> '## Notes' section, both owner-approved. (5) Versions: cloudwatcher 17->18, simulator 2->3, skyalert 10->11. No new files, so no Xcode project change needed. Tests on the built worktree: test_aux_simulator 20 PASS/0 FAIL, test_aux_cloudwatcher_simulator 31 PASS/0 FAIL, test_aux_skyalert_simulator 14 PASS/0 FAIL, test_agent_auxiliary_simulator 5 PASS/0 FAIL, all rc=0. test_aux_skyalert_transport not run (known baseline failure in another ticket). No defects found.
